hazards: High-capacity lithium-ion battery pack posing fire and thermal-runaway risks if damaged
Lead-based solder, brominated flame retardants (BFRs), and beryllium copper on motherboards
Trace mercury in older CCFL-backlit LCD displays and arsenic/cadmium in semiconductors
safe_handling: Back up personal files and securely wipe/reset the storage drive
Power off completely and remove external accessories (USB dongles, SD cards)
Carry and store flat in a dry space without stacking heavy items on the lid
unsafe_actions: Never pry out an internal pouch battery with sharp screwdrivers or metal tools
Do not smash the display screen or burn plastic casings
Never dispose of laptops in municipal solid waste
what_to_do_if_damaged: If the screen is cracked, cover it with clear tape to prevent glass injuries. If the chassis is bulging or hot due to a swollen battery, isolate the laptop in a cool, fire-safe area and hand it directly to trained e-waste staff.
disposal_route: Hand over to an OEM brand take-back center, certified IT asset refurbisher (if working), or a CPCB/SPCB-authorized e-waste recycler.
recoverable_materials: Gold, silver, palladium, and copper (motherboard and connectors)
Neodymium magnets (speakers and cooling fans) and high-grade ABS plastics
environmental_impact: Improper dismantling releases toxic dioxins, heavy metals, and flame retardants into air and water, while wasting high-value precious and rare-earth metals.
